revision_notes: Initial architecture analysis for agent team roster, roles, and access controls.
title: Architecture analysis: Agent team roster with consolidated role registry, universal concurrency, and role-level access control
summary: Define a comprehensive agent roster for the async, self-organizing agent team model. The recommended approach (Option B from refine: Consolidated Role Registry with Category Metadata) adds an AgentCategory enum to classify roles into EXECUTION, ANALYSIS, REVIEW, UTILITY, and INTERFACE categories, consolidates the AgentRole enum from 4 locations to a single canonical source (shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py), adds AUTOFIXER and CONFLICT_RESOLVER as UTILITY roles with gateway patterns, removes remaining integrator test references, and updates documentation to reflect universal concurrency support. The ConcurrentPhaseExecutor and gateway enforcement are already phase-agnostic — the primary work is role registry consolidation, new role addition, and documentation alignment.

approaches_considered.title: Incremental Roster Update
approaches_considered.description: Update existing AgentRole enum in-place across all 4 locations. Add new roles, clean up integrator refs, update docs. Keep multi-location enum pattern.
pros: Minimal disruption — builds on already-functional system
No migration needed for existing 13 roles
cons: Four-location enum remains a sync hazard (already caused INSPECTOR divergence)
No category metadata for dynamic team composition queries
Doesn't address foundational issues for #1028 team framework

approaches_considered.title: Consolidated Role Registry with Category Metadata (RECOMMENDED)
approaches_considered.description: Consolidate AgentRole enum to shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py as single source. Add AgentCategory enum (EXECUTION, ANALYSIS, REVIEW, UTILITY, INTERFACE). All other locations import or re-export. Add new AUTOFIXER and CONFLICT_RESOLVER roles. Clean up integrator refs. Update gateway patterns and documentation.
pros: Single source of truth eliminates sync bugs (fixes INSPECTOR divergence)
Category metadata enables dynamic team composition queries ('all review agents', 'all execution agents')
Cleaner separation of role definition from phase mapping
cons: Requires updating imports across orchestrator and shared packages
Pydantic model validators in orchestrator/models.py need special handling for backward compatibility
More work upfront than Option A

approaches_considered.title: Capability-Based Dynamic Role System
approaches_considered.description: Replace static enum + role-definition with a capability-based system. Roles defined by capabilities (can_write_source, can_review, can_spawn_agents, etc.).
pros: Maximum flexibility for future agent types
Natural fit for dynamic team composition
cons: Significant architectural change with high risk for a specification issue
Overkill for current roster size (15-16 roles)
Gateway enforcement is role-string-based; capability-based requires rearchitecting
Premature abstraction — team model (#1028) still being defined

recommended_approach.title: Consolidated Role Registry with Category Metadata
recommended_approach.justification: This approach was recommended during the refine phase analysis and approved by both the refine reviewer and agent design reviewer. It addresses the root cause of the role divergence problem (INSPECTOR appears only in orchestrator/models.py) while adding the category metadata needed for the #1028 team framework. The scope is manageable and the risk is moderate — the main challenge is updating Pydantic model validators to import from the shared source rather than defining their own enum.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Eliminates the 4-location sync hazard that already caused the INSPECTOR divergence. Other modules import or re-export. orchestrator/models.py gets a compatibility shim: `from egg_contracts.agent_roles import AgentRole` plus any orchestrator-specific roles (INSPECTOR) defined as extensions.

architecture_decisions.decision: New AgentCategory enum with 5 values: EXECUTION, ANALYSIS, REVIEW, UTILITY, INTERFACE
architecture_decisions.rationale: Enables the orchestrator to query roles by category for dynamic team composition (e.g., 'spawn all REVIEW agents for this phase'). Categories are metadata on AgentRoleDefinition, not a separate hierarchy.

architecture_decisions.decision: Add AUTOFIXER and CONFLICT_RESOLVER as UTILITY category roles
architecture_decisions.rationale: These are PR-specific utility agents defined in the issue. They need gateway patterns, role definitions, and file access declarations. They are NOT part of standard pipeline teams — they run independently in response to PR events.

The coordinator role requires elevated permissions (spawn agents, skip phases) that are still being defined in #1028. Adding a placeholder would create ambiguity. The role registry consolidation in this issue makes adding the coordinator in #1028 straightforward.

architecture_decisions.decision: Clean up remaining integrator references in tests
architecture_decisions.rationale: 4 references remain in test files and one gateway comment. These should be removed or updated to use valid role names.

architecture_decisions.decision: No changes to ConcurrentPhaseExecutor or concurrency gates
architecture_decisions.rationale: The executor is already phase-agnostic. get_agent_roles() calls get_roles_for_phase(phase) dynamically. is_concurrent_execution() respects concurrent_phases config. The issue's line references to hardcoded phase checks appear outdated — the code has already been generalized.

INSPECTOR exists only in orchestrator/models.py but not in the canonical source. During consolidation, either add INSPECTOR to the canonical source (if it's a legitimate role) or remove it from models.py (if it's an orchestrator-internal concept). Investigation suggests INSPECTOR is used for health checks and should be added to the canonical source as an INTERFACE category role.

orchestrator/models.py and types.py have a generic REVIEWER role not in the canonical source. This is a legacy catch-all. During consolidation, keep it for backward compatibility in Pydantic validators (deserialized from persisted state) but add migration logic similar to reviewer_unified → reviewer_code.

unresolved_hitl_decisions.question: Tester source-file write access scope
unresolved_hitl_decisions.impact_on_architecture: Affects TESTER_PATTERNS in gateway/agent_restrictions.py. If restricted to test dirs only, tester loses ability to auto-fix lint issues in source files. Recommendation: Keep broad write access (current behavior) until a tester-specific auto-fix workflow is designed.

unresolved_hitl_decisions.question: COORDINATOR role inclusion
unresolved_hitl_decisions.impact_on_architecture: If included, adds a 16th role to the roster with elevated gateway permissions. Recommendation: Defer to #1028 (opt-b). The consolidated registry makes adding it later trivial.

unresolved_hitl_decisions.question: Enum consolidation scope
unresolved_hitl_decisions.impact_on_architecture: Core architectural decision. If consolidated (opt-a), this issue's primary work is the import refactoring. If kept separate with sync test (opt-b), work is smaller but the sync hazard persists. Recommendation: Consolidate (opt-a).

unresolved_hitl_decisions.question: Gateway enforcement default
unresolved_hitl_decisions.impact_on_architecture: If enforce-by-default (opt-a), need to verify all existing roles' patterns are correct before switching. If warn-only (opt-b), shared worktree safety depends on explicit opt-in. Recommendation: Enforce by default (opt-a), but guard with thorough pattern testing.

constraints: Backward compatibility: persisted pipeline state may contain removed role names — migration logic (e.g., _REMOVED_ROLE_MIGRATION) must be maintained
Pydantic model validators: orchestrator/models.py uses AgentRole in Pydantic Field validators — switching to imported enum may affect serialization/deserialization
Gateway security: any new file patterns must follow the 'blocked-first' security model where blocked patterns take precedence over allowed patterns
Test isolation: integrator cleanup in test files must not break unrelated test assertions
